# Commercial Lending Solutions (CLS CRE)

> Commercial mortgage broker headquartered in Los Angeles (7951 Blackburn Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90048; 310.708.0690; loans@clscre.com). Founded by Trevor Damyan, California DRE License #02244836. Arranges construction, permanent, bridge, life insurance company, CMBS and agency loans from $1M to $100M+ through 1,000+ banks, credit unions, life companies, CMBS conduits, debt funds and agency lenders. 46 documented California closings totaling $334M (32 in Los Angeles County); more than $1B in aggregate career volume. BBB accredited (A+); member of ULI and NAIOP.

> Content is written or reviewed by Trevor Damyan. Case studies come from executed loan documents, withhold borrower names, describe lenders by type and use city-level geography. Firm-wide figures ($1B+, 1,000+ lenders) are career totals.

## Legislative Edge — California housing law and deal underwriting

- [Legislative Edge archive](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/): California housing bills and local implementation translated into entitlement, land-basis, capital-stack, and lender decisions
- [Issue 3 — SB 35's 10-unit line](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-3-sb-35/): Ministerial approval, prevailing-wage and affordability thresholds, and small multifamily addition financing
- [Issue 4 — SB 79 day one](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-4-sb-79-day-one/): Why Los Angeles parcel underwriting starts with the local ordinance and ZIMAS map rather than statewide headline density
- [Issue 5 — Measure ULA](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-5-measure-ula/): Full-consideration transfer-tax cliffs, residual value, sale proceeds, and construction/bridge/permanent loan sizing
- [Issue 6: One house. Eight new homes. Nine parcels.](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-6-sb-1123-backyard-stack/): A Van Nuys site went from a three-lot approval to a nine-parcel filing. The capital edge is in the remainder parcel, map clock, and release structure.
- [Issue 7: The final sprint is about whether housing can get financed](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-7-cost-of-capital-bills/): The 2025-26 California legislative session adjourns August 31. The final sprint is not about zoning anymore. It is about whether housing can get financed.
- [Issue 8: The ballot is the capital event](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-8-november-ballot-housing-bond/): California's November 3 ballot is fully set at 14 propositions. Three of them are competing for the same capital: a $11.25B housing bond, a $25B homebuyer program, and an $8.4B research bond.
- [Issue 9: Your empty office is a housing asset. The law just caught up.](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-9-adaptive-reuse-ordinance/): LA's new adaptive-reuse rule (AB 507 + the Citywide Adaptive Reuse Ordinance) lets 15-plus-year-old office buildings convert to housing ministerially. Developers are already acting.
- [Issue 10: Downtown LA's ceiling just moved to 450 feet. The state did it, not the city.](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-10-ab-2074-downtown-high-rise/): The session ended August 31 and the housing package is on the Governor's desk.
- [Issue 11: Eleven housing bills sit with the Governor. On September 30, silence is a signature.](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-11-governors-desk-deadline/): Eleven housing bills sit with the Governor until September 30, and under Article IV, Section 10(b)(2) silence is a signature.
- [Issue 12: The quiet upzone nobody marketed: 16 units on an ordinary R2 lot, and it has been live since June 30.](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-12-sb-79-low-rise-r2-lots/): Since June 30 an LA ordinance has let an ordinary R2 lot near a rail station carry up to 16 units with no parking, no hearing, no bonus paperwork.
- [Issue 17: What a Hollywood Lot Is Really Worth](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/issue-17-100-percent-affordable-stack/): The 100% affordable stack, a vacant lot by the Hollywood/Highland station, and what the dirt is really worth.
- [Briefing: Measure ULA and the November 3 Ballot: What Developers Should Know](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/briefing-measure-ula-ballot-2026/): The ULA rewrite is not on the November 3 ballot. What Prop 43 and Prop TE do, today's $5.4M and $10.9M lines, and the sale vs refi math on a 2028 exit.
- [Briefing: Prop 1's $11.25 Billion Housing Bond: How an LA Developer Would Use It](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/briefing-prop-1-housing-bond-2026/): Where Prop 1's $11.25B housing bond money goes, how it fits a 4% tax credit stack, when HCD funds could flow, and what LA developers should line up now.
- [Briefing: ADUs and Small Lots on January 1, 2027: File Now or Wait?](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/briefing-adu-rules-january-2027/): AB 956, SB 1117 and SB 1116 take effect January 1, 2027. What changes for LA ADUs, JADUs, impact fees and starter home lot splits, and whether to file now.
- [Briefing: The Altadena freeze: what SB 1090 stops and where starter homes still work](https://clscre.com/insights/legislative-edge/briefing-altadena-sb-1090-freeze/): SB 1090 freezes new SB 684 and SB 1123 starter home filings in Altadena ZIPs 91001 and 91003 until 2030. Who is grandfathered, and why January 1 matters.

## Affordable housing & EDI content

- [EDI / ED1 Explained: Ground-Up Affordable Financing in Los Angeles (2026)](https://clscre.com/blog/edi-ed1-ground-up-affordable-financing-los-angeles-2026.html): Cornerstone guide to LA Executive Directive 1 eligibility, incentives, capital stack, timelines, and lender sourcing for 100% affordable ground-up multifamily
- [4% vs 9% LIHTC: Which Does Your Deal Need?](https://clscre.com/blog/4-vs-9-lihtc-which-does-your-deal-need.html): Practical decision framework for choosing between competitive 9% and bond-financed 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits
- [Affordable Housing Development in Los Angeles](https://clscre.com/blog/affordable-housing-developers-los-angeles.html): Market guide covering LAHD funding, entitlement bonuses, prevailing wage, AMI tiers, per-unit development costs
- [LIHTC Tax Credit Financing Explained](https://clscre.com/blog/lihtc-tax-credit-financing-explained.html): Educational primer on 4% and 9% LIHTC mechanics, syndicator dynamics, investor pricing, compliance periods
- [HHAP, NPLH, AHSC, MHP: California's Affordable Housing Capital Stack Decoded](https://clscre.com/blog/california-affordable-housing-capital-stack-hhap-nplh-ahsc-mhp-decoded.html): Field guide to the four state soft-debt programs most California affordable deals need, with stacking strategy and allocation-round timing
- [HUD/FHA for Affordable and Workforce Multifamily: 221(d)(4), 223(f), 220](https://clscre.com/blog/hud-fha-affordable-workforce-multifamily-221d4-223f-220.html): Three HUD/FHA multifamily programs, when each fits, timelines, MAP lender ecosystem
- [Community Benefits Agreements and Mission-Aligned Capital](https://clscre.com/blog/community-benefits-agreements-mission-aligned-capital.html): How CBAs shape affordable deal economics and which mission-driven capital sources underwrite them favorably
- [Land Trust Partnerships and Ground Leases](https://clscre.com/blog/land-trust-partnerships-ground-leases-nonprofit-developers.html): Community land trust and ground-lease affordable housing structures, lender reception, and capital stack implications

## CRE financing comparison library

Side-by-side capital-source, strategy, and structural comparisons. Each comparison page covers pricing, leverage, recourse, prepayment, decision framework, anonymized real CLS CRE deal example, and 7 to 8 FAQs.

- [Comparisons hub](https://clscre.com/comparisons/index.html): All 26+ comparison pages
- Strategy: Acquisition vs Cash-out Refinance, Refinance vs Sell, Bridge to Perm vs Direct Permanent, Construction-to-Perm vs Separate Take-Out, Loan Assumption vs New Loan
- Structural: Recourse vs Non-Recourse, Fixed vs Floating Rate, Interest-Only vs Amortizing, 5-Year Fixed vs 10-Year Fixed, Cross-Collateralization vs Individual Loans
- Asset class: Self-Storage vs Multifamily Investment, Office vs Industrial Cap Rate, STNL vs Multi-Tenant Retail

35+ specialty property type hubs covering institutional sub-types and owner-operator niches with dedicated lender ecosystems.

- Multifamily sub-types: Build-to-Rent (BTR), Manufactured Housing Communities (MHC), Single-Family Rental (SFR) Portfolios, Student Housing, Senior Active Adult 55+, Workforce / NOAH
- Specialty industrial: Cold Storage, Industrial Outdoor Storage (IOS), Manufacturing
- Specialty hospitality: Marina, RV Park / Campground, Truck Stop / Travel Center, Hotel-to-Residential Conversion
- Specialty conversion / adaptive reuse: Office-to-Residential Conversion, Hotel-to-Residential Conversion
- Specialty niche: Boat and RV Storage, Cannabis Dispensary / Cultivation, Charter School, Religious / Church, Skilled Nursing Facility, Independent Living, Land (Entitled)

## Original CRE research

Quarterly publications aggregating CLS CRE active deal pipeline data. Original data, anonymized at the lender level, presented as a primary source for CRE professionals, journalists, researchers, and investors.

- [Research hub](https://clscre.com/research/index.html): All CLS CRE research publications
- [Closed Deal Report Q1 2026](https://clscre.com/research/closed-deal-report-q1-2026.html): Aggregated closed deal volume by vertical, capital source, geography, time-to-close, and deal size
- [Research Methodology](https://clscre.com/research/methodology.html): Data collection, anonymization, sample composition, and statistical approach
